quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the rider leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the rider and lean when the rider leans. Sit forward without crowding the rider. Hold onto the rider's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What blood alcohol concentration (BAC) makes a person legally intoxicated?
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent is the legal intoxication limit. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road. Get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Change your lane position as conditions change.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight.
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position as needed, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see you as easily as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about being seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume others do not see you.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should only be used on wet roads.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes when you slow or stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down if they are leading.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can easily watch them.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should change based on riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Open up your following distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have little experience on their specific motorcycle.

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a single line.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for normal riding. However, when entering or exiting a highway, taking curves, or turning, riders should switch to a single-file line.

questions.question: What clothing gives a motorcyclist the best protection?

options.text: Shoes that do not cover the ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles. Use low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs or the road. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and help you grip the controls better.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts occur between motorcyclists and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing on the left. This position gives you the best view of the road ahead for safe passing.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a motorcycle horn?

options.text: Other drivers usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: A horn is useful for getting attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: For protection, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly reduce throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this may also worsen the wobble.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: Where should you ride if there are hazards on your left?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When there are hazards on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield protects your eyes and face the best. Regular glasses or sunglasses are not enough. In Vermont, you do not have to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still a good idea.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to avoid a crash?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: To reduce your chance of a crash, make yourself visible. Wear bright-colored clothing when you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: For eye or face protection to work well, which is NOT necessary?
questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight.
questions.explanation: Eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist damage, give clear side views, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. They should also fit over glasses or sunglasses. They do NOT need to be airtight.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they look at you.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that other drivers see you, even if they look directly at you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but still do not see them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: One that gives less space and lets others see you.
One that gives more space and lets others see you.
One that increases road hazards and lets others pass you.
One that reduces road hazards and lets you follow closely behind others.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that gives more space and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind from other vehicles, their blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep others from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears. Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you.
